fact: The GPE KIX authors list individual-level data collection among the EMIS's routine exercises as of the February 2025 engagement: information captured on each learner and teacher, such as demographics and performance, with tools that collect it at the school level; the document does not say how often a school enters it.

The document states that the EMIS Unit of the Ministry of Education and Training updated the EMIS data collection instruments and, in February 2025 with HISP Uganda, convened the schools to revise them, with UNICEF supporting the guidelines.

The Minister for Finance states that Government is moving from a paper-based approach to the web-based DHIS2 for Education, designed to capture data on individual learners in Grade 0, primary and high schools, and teachers, by their Personal Identification Numbers.

The Budget Speech 2024 states that data capturing in DHIS2 for Education was at 90%, alongside cleaning and quality assurance, with the Annual Education Census Report targeted for March 2024; it gives no number or share of schools and does not say who captures the data or where.

The Budget Speech 2024 presents DHIS2 for Education as Government's own system, which it says will serve the processing of Free Primary Education grants, the Teaching Service Commission's human resource management and links to other government systems.

The Government Performance Report for November 2023 to September 2024 states that the Ministry of Education and Training launched SEMIS, a real-time web-based system driven by the Personal Identity Number that makes it possible to track learners, developed with the support of education partners; it gives no launch date, so the year of the reporting period's end is used.

The DHIS2 for Education country page states that the Ministry of Education and Training, with UNICEF Eswatini's support, proposed DHIS2 for Education through an initial pilot project in 2020, sought so as to monitor individual learners and staff by personal identification number; it gives no number of pilot schools.

The page states that the country has since expanded to nationwide implementation and gives the scale as National, with no count or share of schools; it gives no date for this, so the document's published year is used.

The page lists the implementation's funding partners as UNICEF Eswatini, GPE KIX, the Ministry of Education and Training and UNESCO Eswatini: the ministry is named as a funder beside three donors, and no budget line or amount is given; undated, so the document's published year is used.
